summary: Phase 3 (FCM subscribe/publish + deep-link) tested. All 8 backend pytest cases pass against the live deploy. Frontend UI, entries list, detail-page sanitization, back navigation, and /entries/:slno deep-link (notification-click simulation) all pass. The subscribe-btn end-to-end flow could NOT be completed inside the Playwright headless Chromium environment because that browser context is incognito-like and Chrome disables the Push API in incognito (crbug.com/401439). The app itself handles this correctly — it surfaces a graceful 'Registration failed - permission denied' error via data-testid='subscribe-error' with no unhandled exceptions. During setup we had to restart the frontend supervisor once because the CRA dev-server had been started before .env was populated with the Firebase config (bundle contained the literal string 'REACT_APP_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID' instead of 'cec-placements23'). After sudo supervisorctl restart frontend the config was baked in correctly.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot be verified end-to-end in Playwright headless Chromium — Push API is disabled in incognito-like contexts (crbug.com/401439). App-side handling verified graceful: subscribe-error chip shows 'Registration failed - permission denied' and no unhandled exception. Backend /api/subscribe was NOT hit because getToken() throws before the POST. Needs verification from a real desktop/mobile browser.

action_items: USER ACTION: verify the 'Enable notifications' button flow from a real Chrome/Firefox tab on desktop or mobile (not incognito, not Playwright headless). Expected: click -> browser permission prompt -> subscribed-chip appears within a few seconds -> devtools Network shows POST /api/subscribe returning 200 with subscribed:true.

OPS NOTE (already applied by testing agent, keep in mind for future): the CRA dev-server bakes REACT_APP_* env vars at start time. If backend/frontend .env is edited, run 'sudo supervisorctl restart frontend' or the runtime bundle will still ship undefined values (leads to 'Installations: Missing App configuration value: projectId' at runtime).

OPTIONAL: consider distinguishing 'Push API unavailable in this browsing context (e.g. incognito)' from a real user-denied permission in the error message rendered in data-testid='subscribe-error', so support/QA can tell them apart. Right now both surface as 'Registration failed - permission denied'.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_phase3_fcm.py — run with `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v`. They hit the live preview deploy (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). If Home.jsx UI changes, note that data-testid='subscribe-btn' is only rendered when Notification.permission !== 'denied' AND user hasn't already subscribed. Playwright headless Chromium reports Notification.permission='denied' even after context.grant_permissions() due to incognito-like context; workaround is to add_init_script overriding Notification.permission getter to return 'granted'. Even then, FCM getToken() will fail because Push API is unavailable in incognito (crbug.com/401439). The subscribe flow must be QA'd manually in a real browser tab.
rca of the issue: Not an app bug. The Playwright automation context runs Chromium in an incognito-like state; Chrome deliberately disables the Push API and reports Notification.permission='denied' regardless of Playwright's grant_permissions() call. FCM's getToken() calls pushManager.subscribe() internally which throws NotAllowedError('permission denied'). The frontend catches this correctly in subscribeToPlacementUpdates() (firebase.js L92-94) and shows a friendly error via data-testid='subscribe-error'. To reproduce a real subscribe, use a real desktop Chrome tab (not headless, not incognito), open the site, click 'Enable notifications', accept the browser prompt. On the backend side, /api/subscribe is confirmed working (rejects garbage tokens with structured 200/502, never a 500).
